final_qi.question: Which protein, by interacting with CD3EAP, POLR1E, and POLR1D, is associated with causing Treacher Collins syndrome?
final_qi.long_answer: Treacher Collins syndrome results from defects in proteins required for ribosomal RNA synthesis. The small subunit common to RNA polymerases I and III—POLR1C (DNA-directed RNA polymerase I and III subunit C)—physically associates with other Pol I components, including CD3EAP (also called ASE-1), POLR1E and POLR1D, to form the functional transcription complex. Pathogenic loss-of-function mutations in the POLR1C gene disrupt this interaction network, impair rRNA transcription, and are a well-established cause of Treacher Collins syndrome (designated TCS type 3). Hence, the protein that interacts with CD3EAP, POLR1E and POLR1D and whose mutation produces Treacher Collins syndrome is POLR1C.

Section: Genetics
TCOF1 is found on the 5th chromosome in the 5q32 region. It codes for a relatively simple nucleolar protein called treacle, that is thought to be involved in ribosome assembly.[18] Mutations in TCOF1 lead to haploinsufficiency of the treacle protein.[24] Haploinsufficiency occurs when a diploid organism has only one functional copy of a gene, because the other copy is inactivated by a mutation. The one normal copy of the gene does not produce enough protein, causing disease. Haploinsufficiency of the treacle protein leads to a depletion of the neural crest cell precursor, which leads to a reduced number of crest cells migrating to the first and second pharyngeal arches. These cells play an important role in the development of the craniofacial appearance, and loss of one copy of treacle affects the cells' ability to form the bones and tissues of the face.[12][20][25] POLR1C and POLR1D mutations are responsible for a minority of cases of Treacher Collins. POLR1C is found on chromosome 6 at position 6q21.2 and POLR1D is found on chromosome 13 at position 13q12.2. Those genes code for a protein subunits shared between RNA polymerase I and III. Both of these polymerases are important for ribosome biogenesis.[12]

Both of these polymerases are important for ribosome biogenesis.[12]

final_answer.long_answer: Treacher Collins syndrome results from defects in proteins required for ribosomal RNA synthesis. The small subunit common to RNA polymerases I and III—POLR1C (DNA-directed RNA polymerase I and III subunit C)—physically associates with other Pol I components, including CD3EAP (also called ASE-1), POLR1E and POLR1D, to form the functional transcription complex. Pathogenic loss-of-function mutations in the POLR1C gene disrupt this interaction network, impair rRNA transcription, and are a well-established cause of Treacher Collins syndrome (designated TCS type 3). Hence, the protein that interacts with CD3EAP, POLR1E and POLR1D and whose mutation produces Treacher Collins syndrome is POLR1C.
